subject: SLA carve-out request — filter/toolchain edgecases & structured-output validation
messages:
From: Procurement - Acme Health <procurement@acmehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops-team@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carve-out language for filter/tool-calls/structured-output failures

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and our engineering ops team have a few contract asks around SLAs we need to reconcile before we move to signature. Because we run in a regulated environment and sometimes pass PHI through tool-calls and structured outputs, we want explicit carve-outs so that certain failures (filter-triggered rejections, 3rd-party tool-calling outages, and structured-output validation failures) are excluded from uptime/latency SLA calculations and credit formulas.

High level asks:
- If a Redwood content filter blocks or redacts a request because of PHI/eligibility, that incident should not count toward uptime/latency SLA once Acme has submitted required evidence for the event.
- If a tool-calling invocation fails due to an external partner (e.g., DocToolInc API outage) or network-level third-party failure, those failures should be treated as carve-outs, provided Redwood shows trace IDs and provider incident tickets.
- If a response is returned but fails our structured-output schema validation (validated client-side), we want a path where these validation errors are classified as functional mismatches rather than service outages if the model produced an answer within latency thresholds.

We attached a short sample of filter error logs and a redline template. Can you propose specific contract language and the operational evidence you need from us (logs, redaction details, trace ids) to mark an incident as exempt? Also need an explicit monthly cap (or other guardrails).

Next steps: please send proposed carve-out language and any alternate mitigations (fallback model, caching behavior, dedicated capacity options).

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Procurement, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

Attachments: Acme_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf, filter-error-samples.csv

Subject: Re: Request: carve-out language for filter/tool-calls/structured-output failures

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear note and the attached logs. I kicked this over to our legal/infra leads for redlines; below is an operational-first proposal we can iterate on. I focused on definitions and minimal operational evidence so we can avoid lengthy back-and-forths.

Proposed carve-out bullets (draft):
1) Definitions: 
   - "Filter-triggered incident": any request that is blocked, truncated, or materially altered by Redwood's content moderation/filtering pipeline such that returned output is not the originally requested model response.
   - "Tool-calling outage": any failed invocation of a third-party tool integrated via Redwood tool-calling where the failure is demonstrably caused by the third-party provider or external network (not by Redwood's runtime).
   - "Structured-output validation failure": a response that does not match an agreed schema but is nevertheless delivered within the latency SLO.

2) Exemption mechanics:
   - Incidents that meet the definition above and are accompanied by Redwood trace IDs, filter logs, and provider incident tickets will be excluded from uptime and p95/p99 latency calculations for SLA credit eligibility for the duration of the incident window.
   - Customers must provide, within 14 days, any additional evidence requested to validate PHI-related filtering decisions (redacted where necessary).

3) Guardrails:
   - Carve-outs are limited to a maximum of 12 exempt incidents per 30-day period, or 0.5% of total request volume in the period, whichever is less.
   - Redwood will provide incident-level metadata (trace IDs, timestamps, sample input hashes) in the incident report.

4) Mitigations & fallbacks (recommended):
   - Automatic model fallback to a compatible variant when a filter triggers; where fallback changes response shape, this is considered a functional change but not necessarily a service outage.
   - Retries/backoff for transient third-party tool errors with exponential backoff for up to 3 attempts before marking as a carve-out.
   - Option: Customers requiring stricter uptime can run on Dedicated capacity or a private deployment with narrower carve-out allowances.

If this looks acceptable at a principle level, Marissa can drop in contract-safe language and add the piece about evidence retention (we typically keep full traces for 90 days by default but can extend as an add-on). Vivek — can you confirm whether trace IDs and provider tickets are sufficient evidence from an infra perspective?

Rachel

Rachel / Vivek — thanks for the draft. I've redlined the contract language and added measurable definitions and evidence requirements. Key internal notes below (copying Acme for visibility):

Edits / clarifications: 
- Formalize the "incident window" as the period from the first failure event timestamp to the time remediation is confirmed in our incident system. Customers may request a start time no earlier than the first recorded failure we can validate.
- For filter-triggered incidents involving potential PHI, we will require (a) the Redwood filter log entry showing the trigger reason, (b) a redacted sample of the input that demonstrates PHI, and (c) a short explanation of remediation steps taken. Redwood retains full logs for 90 days; we can extend to 180 days for enterprise customers with a retention add-on.
- For tool-calling outages, carve-outs will be granted only when a corresponding provider incident ticket (or public status page incident) is provided AND Redwood internal traces show the external call returned a non-2xx status or timed out.
- Structured-output validation failures: if the model returns an output that fails schema validation but the response was returned within the p95 latency boundary, classify as a "functional mismatch" (not an SLA outage) unless the schema failure was caused by malformed input attributable to Redwood processing.

SLA math / credits: 
- Suggest limiting credits to non-exempt incidents only. Exempt incidents should not reduce the number of non-exempt incidents used in credit calculations.
- Recommend a monthly cap to avoid abuse: 12 exempt incidents / 30 days or 0.5% of requests — whichever is smaller.

Operational evidence / auditability: 
- Required metadata for any carve-out claim: trace_id, request_timestamp, endpoint, model_id, filter_rule_id (if applicable), and any provider incident ticket identifiers.
- Redwood will provide an incident packet within 48 hours of a carve-out request with the above fields.

Fallbacks & options: 
- If Acme requires stricter guarantees we recommend Dedicated capacity; carve-out allowances are narrower for Dedicated. (We should specify the narrower cap in the Dedicated SOW.)

I've attached the redlined PDF (Acme_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf) with inline comments. Rachel — if you OK the language I can produce a final redline for signature that integrates these evidence requirements.

Marissa Cole
Head, Product Security & Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

2) We want the carve-out cap to be applied per environment (prod vs staging) — prod has 12 exempt incidents / 30 days, staging unlimited.

We accept the rest of the proposed language, including the evidence set and the definition of structured-output validation failures. We'll sign once you update the redline to reflect the 24-hour packet delivery and the per-environment cap. Also please add a single sentence that clarifies third-party tool providers referenced in the carve-out are limited to identified integrations in Exhibit B (we'll attach a vendor list).
